title: Sequential Outlier Detection in Non-Stationary Time
Sequential Outlier Detection in Non-Stationary Time Series
summary: The paper addresses sequential outlier detection in time series whose mean can drift, where repeated tests inflate false-positive probabilities. It estimates the mean with a one-sided local-linear smoother plus Jackknife bias reduction, then uses extreme-value theory to set GEV-based critical values for the maximum residual over n consecutive tests. In simulations and Australian temperature data, the full and partial procedures achieve high specificity and competitive sensitivity, with the full IID μ1 n=50 standard-normal setting reporting 98.3% specificity.

why: The authors' repository contains a pure NumPy/SciPy implementation of the proposed full method (called 'sequential' in code), and C1 is a synthetic no-outlier simulation cell that needs no external data or weights. The core run should work on Python 3.12 after installing standard scientific packages and avoiding optional competitor-method imports (rpy2/tensorflow/river), which are not needed for C1.
est_runtime: About 10-15 minutes with 22-core parallelization over series; roughly 25-30 minutes if the authors' code is run single-process.
blockers: No requirements.txt/pyproject; core dependencies must be installed manually (numpy, scipy, pandas, matplotlib, tueplots).
alternative_methods.py imports optional rpy2/tensorflow/river for competitor methods; these are not needed for C1 and may be unavailable on Windows/Python 3.12.

approach: Reproduce the matched target C1 only: the proposed full method on 1,000 no-outlier IID standard-normal series rescaled to mean 0 and sd 1/20, mean function μ1, n=50, horizon 11n=550. The implementation will be a thin wrapper around the authors' pure NumPy/SciPy code, calling experiments.sequential_test (the code's name for the full method) and data_generation.py for μ1 rather than rewriting the estimator. reproduce.py will seed all stochastic steps, parallelize over series, pool decisions on indices n+1..11n, compute 100*TN/(TN+FP), and write results/metrics.json checked against 98.3% ± 1.0 percentage point. Optional C2-C5 can reuse the same wrapper only if the C1 run finishes well inside budget; C6-C8 need external BOM data and are out of scope for the matched target.
steps: Clone the authors' repository if it is not already present: git clone https://github.com/FlorianHeinrichs/outlier_detection.git and cd into it.

Install core dependencies with python -m pip: numpy scipy pandas matplotlib tueplots tqdm. Do not install or import competitor stacks for C1 unless required by an author import; if experiments.py imports alternative_methods and that fails on optional rpy2/tensorflow/river, add a minimal sys.modules/import shim in reproduce.py or c1_runner.py rather than editing author files.

Inspect experiments.py, data_generation.py, experiments_config.py, jackknife.py, and quantiles.py to read exact function signatures, the μ1 generator, default bandwidth grid, GEV fitting code, and whether sequential_test is the full method. Record the actual call signature in c1_runner.py.

Implement c1_runner.py: a function run_one_series(series_seed) that calls the authors' data generator for μ1 with IID N(0,1) errors rescaled to mean 0 and sd 1/20, no outliers, length 550; calls experiments.sequential_test with alpha=0.01, full estimator, quartic kernel, 5-fold CV bandwidth; returns a boolean rejection array for indices n+1..11n.

Implement reproduce.py: parse --smoke (5 series) versus default (1000 series); set base seed 0 and deterministic per-series seeds; parallelize over series with multiprocessing.Pool using an if __name__ == '__main__' guard; collect rejection counts.

Run a smoke test on 5 series before touching the full run: python reproduce.py --smoke. Confirm data shapes, finite residuals, finite GEV fits, a selected bandwidth inside the grid, and exactly 5*500=2500 test decisions.
Run the full C1 experiment with python reproduce.py. Use min(16, cpu_count) workers; save optional per-series rejection counts to results/c1_per_series.csv for audit.
Aggregate specificity by pooling all normal test decisions: specificity_percent = 100 * (1 - total_rejections / (n_series * (11*n - n))). For C1 the denominator is 1000*500 = 500,000 test points.

Write results/metrics.json with claim_id C1, metric specificity_percent, value, paper_value 98.3, tolerance_abs 1.0, unit %, n, horizon, n_series, test_points, alpha, seed, runtime, selected-bandwidth summary, and status reproduced/not_reproduced if abs(value-98.3)<=1.0.

Check the tolerance. If outside 1.0 point, run diagnostics only: verify full-vs-partial function choice, GEV shape sign, use of rolling vs disjoint maxima, exclusion of first n from the metric, bandwidth CV split, and seed handling. Do not tune undocumented choices to hit the paper value; document any unresolved discrepancy.

If C1 passes and more than 15 minutes remain, optionally run C2-C5 via the same wrapper with n=200 or contaminated settings using A7 for outlier heights. Otherwise stop; C6-C8 are out of scope because they require external BOM data.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke. This runs 5 series, n=50, horizon=550, no outliers, and should finish in about 1-2 minutes on CPU. Success criteria: generated series are finite and length 550; GEV fit finite; selected bandwidth is within the configured grid; exactly 2500 rejection decisions are produced; results/metrics.json is written. The smoke specificity is not required to be within 1.0 of 98.3, only the data flow must be proven.
intermediate_checks: After install, verify imports without competitor stacks: python -c "import experiments, data_generation; print('ok')" after any optional-import shim; if this fails, resolve import errors before writing the runner.
Confirm in experiments.py that sequential_test is the full all-observations-up-to-i method and partial_test is the partial method; the README wording is ambiguous, so check the code/docstring.
Generate one μ1 no-outlier series and check shape (550,), no NaNs/infs, empirical sd close to 0.05 after rescaling, and that μ1 is not constant.
Run one series through c1_runner.py and check rejection flags are boolean and have length 500 after excluding the first n=50 observations.
Inspect one GEV calibration: quantile finite, shape parameter not absurd, rolling maxima count equals n-r+1 for r=floor(sqrt(50))=7, and selected bandwidth h is one of the grid values.
Check the full-run denominator is 1000*(11*50-50)=500,000 test points for C1; expected non-rejections at 98.3% is about 491,500.

Run a sanity baseline on 10-20 series before the full run: no-outlier specificity should be high (roughly >95%); if it is near 0% or 100%, suspect reversed GEV shape sign, wrong quantile, including first n in the metric, or a broken bandwidth CV.

Check the distribution of CV-selected bandwidths across a small subset; if essentially all at the grid boundary, note it and use the authors' default grid if available rather than expanding the grid ad hoc.
Before the full run, time the smoke run and estimate full runtime as (n_series/smoke_n_series) times smoke per-series cost; adjust workers to keep within budget.
budget_plan: Setup (clone if needed, pip install, import shim inspection): ~5-8 minutes. Smoke run (5 series): ~2-3 minutes. Full C1 run (1000 series, n=50, horizon=550): ~15-25 minutes with 8-16 workers, or ~25-30 minutes single-process if multiprocessing is unstable. Aggregation and metrics.json: ~1 minute. Keep ~5 minutes buffer for import issues and tolerance diagnostics. Do not start optional C2-C5 until C1 has produced metrics.json inside tolerance and at least ~15 minutes remain; C6-C8 are explicitly skipped in this budget because they require external BOM data.

   50| def mu_1(n: int, a: float = 1.) -> np.ndarray:
   51|     """
   52|     Generates a non-monotonically decreasing function (defined on the unit
   53|     interval).
   54| 
   55|     :param n: Number of supporting points (observations).
   56|     :param a: Scaling parameter for quadratic term.
   57|     :return: Function values at points np.arange(n) / n
   58|     """
   59|     x = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
   60|     mu = a * (x - 1 / 2) ** 2 + np.sin(5 * 2 * np.pi * x) / 10 + 3/4

   62|     return mu.reshape((1, n))

   67|     Generates a monotonically decreasing function (defined on the unit

   70|     :param n: Number of supporting points (observations).

   75|     mu[(3 * n) // 4:] = 1
   76|     mu = mu / 4 + 0.75

def calculate_confusion_matrix(real_outliers, test_decision) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Calculate confusion matrix based on detected and real outliers.

:param real_outliers: NumPy array containing indices of real outliers.
    :param test_decision: NumPy array containing the test decision (0 or 1) of
        size (n_time_series, m_remaining).
    :return: Confusion matrix based on detected and real outliers.
    """
    real = np.zeros_like(test_decision, dtype=bool)
    index = np.expand_dims(np.arange(len(test_decision)), axis=-1)
    real[index, real_outliers] = True

    tp = np.sum(test_decision * real, axis=-1)
    tn = np.sum((1 - test_decision) * (1 - real), axis=-1)
    fn = np.sum(real * (1 - test_decision), axis=-1)
    fp = np.sum((1 - real) * test_decision, axis=-1)

    confusion_matrix = np.array([[tp, fn],
                                 [fp, tn]])
    confusion_matrix = np.transpose(confusion_matrix, axes=[2, 0, 1])

    return confusion_matrix

#
# c1_runner.py
#
# Per-series runner for claim C1 of the reproduction:
#   Empirical specificity of the proposed FULL method for IID standard normal
#   errors, mean function mu1, n = 50, horizon 11n = 550, no outliers.
#
# This is a thin wrapper around the authors' released code
# (https://github.com/FlorianHeinrichs/outlier_detection):
#   - data_generation.generate_data  -> mu1 + IID N(0, 1) rescaled to sd 1/20
#   - jackknife.bandwidth_cv         -> 5-fold CV bandwidth on first n points
#   - experiments.parallel_test      -> the paper's "full" method
#
# The paper's "full" version uses the estimator based on ALL observations up
# to time i (paper p. 9); in the authors' code that is parallel_test, while
# sequential_test masks previously detected outliers ("partial" version).
#
# The authors' experiments.py imports alternative_methods.py at module level,
# which needs river/rpy2/tensorflow (competitor methods). Those are NOT needed
# for the proposed method, so we inject a stub module before importing.

import os
import sys
import types

import numpy as np

REPO_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "repo")
if REPO_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, REPO_DIR)


def _install_alternative_methods_shim() -> None:
    """
    Stub out the authors' alternative_methods module so that importing
    experiments.py does not require the optional competitor stacks
    (river, rpy2, tensorflow), which are irrelevant for the proposed method.
    """
    if "alternative_methods" in sys.modules:
        return
    try:
        import alternative_methods  # noqa: F401
        return
    except Exception:
        pass

    stub = types.ModuleType("alternative_methods")

    def _unused(*args, **kwargs):
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Competitor methods are not available (river/rpy2/tensorflow not "
            "installed); they are not needed for the proposed method."
        )

    stub.campulova_2018 = _unused
    stub.holesovsky_2018 = _unused
    stub.ml_based = _unused
    sys.modules["alternative_methods"] = stub


_install_alternative_methods_shim()

import experiments as authors_experiments          # noqa: E402
import data_generation as authors_data_generation  # noqa: E402
import jackknife as authors_jackknife              # noqa: E402

# Paper Section 3.1: joint level alpha for n consecutive tests = 1%.
ALPHA = 0.01
# Paper Section 3.1: errors rescaled to mean 0 and standard deviation 1/20.
SIGMA = 1.0 / 20.0
# Authors' CV settings (experiments_config.py / _v2.py: CV_KWARGS).
CV_KWARGS = {"num_folds": 5, "min_bw": 2, "max_bw": 20}
# One-sided quartic kernel K(x) = 15/8 (1 - x^2)^2 on [-1, 0] is the kernel
# implemented by the authors' jackknife.get_kernel (quartic, support [-1, 0]).
# The bandwidth grid / folds / kernel therefore all follow the authors' code.


def generate_one_series(seed: int, n_total: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    One no-outlier time series: X_i = mu1(i/n) + eps_i, eps ~ N(0, (1/20)^2).

    Uses the authors' data generator. The authors' generate_iid draws from an
    unseeded np.random.default_rng(); for reproducibility we inject a seeded
    generator for the duration of the call. The legacy global RNG is seeded as
    well because bandwidth_cv shuffles CV folds with np.random.shuffle.
    """
    import unittest.mock

    original_default_rng = np.random.default_rng
    np.random.seed(seed)
    with unittest.mock.patch.object(
            np.random, "default_rng",
            lambda seed=None: original_default_rng(seed)):
        data = authors_data_generation.generate_data(
            mean_type="1",
            mean_kwargs={"n": n_total, "a": 1},
            error_type="iid",
            error_kwargs={"n": n_total, "n_samples": 1,
                          "distribution": "normal", "sigma": SIGMA},
        )
    return data


def run_one_series(seed: int, n_stable: int = 50, n_factor: int = 11,
                   alpha: float = ALPHA) -> dict:
    """
    Run the authors' full method on one simulated no-outlier series.

    :param seed: Per-series seed (deterministic).
    :param n_stable: n, the length of the outlier-free initial period used
        for bandwidth selection and GEV estimation (paper: n = 50).
    :param n_factor: Horizon factor; series length is n_factor * n_stable
        (paper: 11n = 550).
    :param alpha: Joint level for the n consecutive tests (paper: 1%).
    :return: Dictionary with counts of false positives (all test points are
        normal in C1), number of test points, bandwidth and GEV estimates.
    """
    n_total = n_factor * n_stable
    m_remaining = n_total - n_stable

    data = generate_one_series(seed, n_total)

    # 5-fold CV bandwidth on the initial outlier-free period (authors' grid).
    bw = authors_jackknife.bandwidth_cv(data[..., :n_stable], **CV_KWARGS)

    quantile_kwargs = {"alpha": alpha * np.ones(m_remaining),
                       "return_estimates": True}

    # Full method: estimator based on all observations up to time i.
    reject_null, mu, sigma, gamma = authors_experiments.parallel_test(
        data, bw, n_stable, quantile_kwargs)

    reject_null = np.asarray(reject_null, dtype=bool).ravel()
    fp = int(np.sum(reject_null))          # every test point is normal in C1
    tn = int(m_remaining - fp)

    return {
        "seed": int(seed),
        "fp": fp,
        "tn": tn,
        "n_test_points": int(m_remaining),
        "bw": int(np.asarray(bw).ravel()[0]),
        "gev_mu": float(np.asarray(mu).ravel()[0]),
        "gev_sigma": float(np.asarray(sigma).ravel()[0]),
        "gev_gamma": float(np.asarray(gamma).ravel()[0]),
    }

#
# reproduce.py
#
# Reproduction of claim C1 of "Sequential Outlier Detection in Non-Stationary
# Time Series" (Heinrichs, Bastian, Dette; arXiv 2502.18038):
#
#   Empirical specificity of the proposed FULL method for IID standard normal
#   errors, mean function mu1, n = 50, no outliers, 1,000 simulated series,
#   horizon 11n = 550 time points, alpha = 1%.
#
# The claim corresponds to Table 1, Panel A (Specificity for mu1),
# row "Ours (full)", n = 50, error distribution N.
#
# Everything is computed with the authors' released code
# (https://github.com/FlorianHeinrichs/outlier_detection):
#   - data_generation.generate_data : X_i = mu1(i/n) + eps_i,
#     eps_i ~ N(0,1) rescaled to mean 0 and sd 1/20 (paper Sec. 3.1)
#   - jackknife.bandwidth_cv        : 5-fold CV bandwidth, MSE loss,
#     integer grid 2..20 (authors' CV_KWARGS), on the first n = 50 points
#   - experiments.parallel_test     : the "full" version (estimator uses ALL
#     observations up to time i), one-sided quartic kernel on [-1, 0],
#     Jackknife bias reduction, GEV threshold from the first n residuals
#     (sliding block maxima, r = ceil(sqrt(n)), PWM estimators) at level
#     alpha = 1% for the n consecutive tests.
#
# Specificity is aggregated per point, as in the authors' "per_point"
# statistics: specificity = 100 * TN / (TN + FP), with TN and FP pooled over
# all series and all test points i = n+1, ..., 11n (500 points per series).
#
# Usage:
#   python reproduce.py            # full run: 1,000 series
#   python reproduce.py --smoke    # smoke run: 5 series
#
# Runtime for the full run is well under one minute (a single series needs
# ~0.02 s), so no parallelization is required.

import argparse
import csv
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import warnings

import numpy as np

from c1_runner import (ALPHA, CV_KWARGS, SIGMA, generate_one_series,
                       run_one_series)

# Claim contract tolerance for C1 (percentage points).
TOLERANCE_ABS = 1.0

# Path of the claim contract shipped with the reproduction (used only to look
# up the paper's reported value for comparison; the computed value below is
# never taken from it).
CONTRACT_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                             "state", "claim_contract.json")


def parse_args(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Reproduce claim C1 (specificity, full method, mu1, "
                    "IID N(0,1) errors, n=50, no outliers).")
    parser.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true",
                        help="Smoke test with 5 series instead of 1,000.")
    parser.add_argument("--n-series", type=int, default=1000,
                        help="Number of simulated time series (paper: 1,000).")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0,
                        help="Base seed; series i uses seed base_seed + i.")
    parser.add_argument("--n-stable", type=int, default=50,
                        help="n, length of outlier-free initial period.")
    parser.add_argument("--n-factor", type=int, default=11,
                        help="Horizon factor; series length is n_factor*n.")
    parser.add_argument("--alpha", type=float, default=ALPHA,
                        help="Joint level alpha for the n consecutive tests.")
    parser.add_argument("--mu1-single-sine", action="store_true",
                        help="Diagnostic: use the paper text's mu1 (one sine "
                             "period over the horizon) instead of the authors'"
                             " data_generation.mu_1 (five periods).")
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def paper_value_from_contract() -> float:
    """
    Read the paper's reported value for C1 from the claim contract shipped in
    state/ (Table 1 Panel A, row 'Ours (full)', n=50, column N is the first
    number of the quote). Returns NaN if unavailable.
    """
    try:
        with open(CONTRACT_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            contract = json.load(f)
        quote = contract["claims"][0]["quote"]
        token = quote.split("Ours (full)")[1].split()[0]
        return float(token)
    except Exception:

def run_series_range(seeds, n_stable, n_factor, alpha, mu1_single_sine=False):
    """Run the full method on one simulated series per seed."""
    if mu1_single_sine:

        # (1 sine period over the horizon) while keeping everything else from
        # the authors' code. Not used for the default run.
        original_mu1 = __import__("data_generation").mu_1

        def mu1_single(n, a=1.0):
            x = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
            return (a * (x - 1 / 2) ** 2
                    + np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) / 10 + 3 / 4).reshape((1, n))

        import data_generation as dg
        dg.mu_1 = mu1_single
        try:

                                   n_factor=n_factor, alpha=alpha)
                    for s in seeds]
        finally:
            dg.mu_1 = original_mu1
        return rows

    return [run_one_series(seed=s, n_stable=n_stable, n_factor=n_factor,
                           alpha=alpha) for s in seeds]

    """
    Calculate confusion matrix based on detected and real outliers.

    :param real_outliers: NumPy array containing indices of real outliers.
    :param test_decision: NumPy array containing the test decision (0 or 1) of
        size (n_time_series, m_remaining).

    """
    real = np.zeros_like(test_decision, dtype=bool)
    index = np.expand_dims(np.arange(len(test_decision)), axis=-1)
    real[index, real_outliers] = True

    tp = np.sum(test_decision * real, axis=-1)
    tn = np.sum((1 - test_decision) * (1 - real), axis=-1)
    fn = np.sum(real * (1 - test_decision), axis=-1)
    fp = np.sum((1 - real) * test_decision, axis=-1)

    confusion_matrix = np.array([[tp, fn],
                                 [fp, tn]])
    confusion_matrix = np.transpose(confusion_matrix, axes=[2, 0, 1])

    return confusion_matrix

       heights = min_height * U(1, 2) with random sign, where
       min_height = get_minimal_height(n, 'normal', std=1/20) is the

            outliers_index = np.stack([
                np.random.choice(np.arange(m_remaining), size=n_outliers,
                                 replace=False) + n_stable
                for _ in range(1)])
            outlier_heights = min_height * np.random.uniform(
                1, 2, size=(1, n_outliers))
            outlier_sign = 2 * np.random.randint(0, 2, (1, n_outliers)) - 1

            data[np.arange(1)[:, None], outliers_index] += outliers

def quote_value_from_contract(claim_index: int, n_stable: int) -> float:
    """
    Look up the paper's reported value for a claim from the claim contract
    shipped in state/. The quotes list 15 numbers: 5 error distributions
    (N, U, Exp, Par1, Par2) for n=50, then n=100, then n=200. The first
    column (N) is what this reproduction targets. Returns NaN if unavailable.
    """
    n_block = {50: 0, 100: 1, 200: 2}.get(n_stable, 0)
    idx = 5 * n_block
    try:
        with open(CONTRACT_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            contract = json.load(f)
        quote = contract["claims"][claim_index]["quote"]
        tokens = quote.split("Ours (full)")[1].split()[:15]
        return float(tokens[idx])
    except Exception:
        return float("nan")


def write_series_csv(path: str, rows: list) -> None:
    with open(path, "w", newline="") as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f)
        writer.writerow(["seed", "true_positives", "false_negatives",
                         "false_positives", "true_negatives",
                         "n_test_points", "bandwidth", "gev_mu", "gev_sigma",
                         "gev_gamma"])
        for r in rows:
            writer.writerow([r["seed"], r["tp"], r["fn"], r["fp"], r["tn"],
                             r["n_test_points"], r["bw"],
                             f"{r['gev_mu']:.6f}", f"{r['gev_sigma']:.6f}",
                             f"{r['gev_gamma']:.6f}"])


def aggregate_claim(claim_id, n_stable, with_outliers, rows, n_series,
                    n_factor, alpha, quote_idx):
    """Aggregate one claim from per-series rows and build its result dict."""
    TP = int(sum(r["tp"] for r in rows))
    FN = int(sum(r["fn"] for r in rows))
    FP = int(sum(r["fp"] for r in rows))
    TN = int(sum(r["tn"] for r in rows))
    n_total = n_factor * n_stable

    if with_outliers:
        metric = "sensitivity"
        value = 100.0 * TP / (TP + FN)
        metric_note = (f"100*TP/(TP+FN) = 100*{TP}/{TP + FN} "
                       f"(outliers detected among "
                       f"{n_series}*int(0.05*{n_total - n_stable}) outlier "
                       f"points)")
    else:
        metric = "specificity"
        value = 100.0 * TN / (TN + FP)
        metric_note = f"100*TN/(TN+FP) = 100*{TN}/{TN + FP}"

    paper_value = quote_value_from_contract(quote_idx, n_stable)
    if np.isfinite(paper_value):
        comparison = {
            "paper_value_reference": paper_value,
            "abs_difference": round(abs(value - paper_value), 3),
            "tolerance_abs": TOLERANCE_ABS,
            "status": ("reproduced"
                       if abs(value - paper_value) <= TOLERANCE_ABS
                       else "not_reproduced"),
        }
    else:
        comparison = {"paper_value_reference": None, "abs_difference": None,
                      "tolerance_abs": TOLERANCE_ABS,
                      "status": "computed (paper value unavailable)"}

    fps = np.array([r["fp"] for r in rows])
    return {
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "metric": metric,
        "value": round(value, 2),
        "unit": f"% {metric}",
        "higher_is_better": True,
        "dataset": (
            "Simulated IID standard normal time series, mean function mu1"
            + (" with 5% outliers (distribution-specific minimal height "
               "times a random factor from U[-2,-1] u [1,2], authors' "
               "outlier generation)" if with_outliers else
               ", no outliers")
            + " (generated with the authors' data_generation.py)"),
        "split": (f"{n_series} simulated time series; horizon "
                  f"{n_factor}n={n_total} time points; test points "
                  f"i=n+1..{n_factor}n ({n_total - n_stable} per series)"),
        "config": {
            "n": n_stable, "n_factor": n_factor, "horizon": n_total,
            "n_series": n_series,
            "test_points_per_series": n_total - n_stable,
            "outlier_rate": 0.05 if with_outliers else 0.0,
            "error_distribution": "IID N(0,1) rescaled to mean 0 and sd "
                                  f"{SIGMA:.4f} (=1/20)",
            "mean_function": "mu1 (authors' data_generation.mu_1, a=1)",
            "kernel": "one-sided quartic K(x)=15/8 (1-x^2)^2 on [-1,0]",
            "estimator": "Jackknife local linear, full version (all "
                         "observations up to time i)",
            "bandwidth_selection": {
                "method": "5-fold cross-validation, MSE loss",
                "num_folds": CV_KWARGS["num_folds"],
                "min_bw": CV_KWARGS["min_bw"], "max_bw": CV_KWARGS["max_bw"]},
            "alpha": alpha,
            "gev": "sliding block maxima, block size ceil(sqrt(n)), PWM, "
                   "extrapolation to block size n (authors' quantiles.py)",
            "seed_base": 0,
        },
        "results": {
            "true_positives": TP, "false_negatives": FN,
            "false_positives": FP, "true_negatives": TN,
            "mean_false_positives_per_series":
                round(float(fps.mean()), 3),
            "bandwidth_median": float(np.median([r["bw"] for r in rows])),
        },
        "comparison_with_paper": comparison,
        "notes": f"Full method ('Ours (full)'), computed per point: "
                 f"{metric_note}. Paper cell: "
                 f"{'Table 2' if with_outliers else 'Table 1'} "
                 f"({'Panel E' if metric == 'sensitivity' else 'Panel A'}), "
                 f"row 'Ours (full)', n={n_stable}, column N.",
    }

def quote_value_from_contract(claim_index: int, n_stable: int) -> float:
    """
    Look up the paper's reported value for a claim from the claim contract
    shipped in state/. The quotes list 15 numbers: 5 error distributions
    (N, U, Exp, Par1, Par2) for n=50, then n=100, then n=200. The first
    column (N) is what this reproduction targets. Returns NaN if unavailable.
    """
    n_block = {50: 0, 100: 1, 200: 2}.get(n_stable, 0)
    idx = 5 * n_block
    try:
        with open(CONTRACT_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            contract = json.load(f)
        quote = contract["claims"][claim_index]["quote"]
        tokens = quote.split("Ours (full)")[1].split()[:15]
        return float(tokens[idx])
    except Exception:
        return float("nan")

    Returns (data, bandwidth, outliers_index_in_test_window_or_None).

    original_default_rng = np.random.default_rng
    np.random.seed(seed)

import experiments as authors_experiments          # noqa: E402
import data_generation as authors_data_generation  # noqa: E402
import jackknife as authors_jackknife              # noqa: E402
import quantiles as authors_quantiles              # noqa: E402

# --- SciPy compatibility shim ----------------------------------------------
# The authors' quantiles.solve_equations() calls scipy.optimize.newton with
# np.ones(np.sum(ind)) as the starting point. For series whose sliding block
# maxima all fall in the Gumbel regime (ind empty) this start array is empty
# and modern SciPy raises "The truth value of an empty array is ambiguous" on
# its internal `if fval == 0` check. The authors' intent in that case is a
# no-op (gamma keeps its closed-form initialisation of 0), so we wrap newton
# to return the empty array unchanged; non-empty inputs are delegated to
# SciPy unchanged, so all non-degenerate series are unaffected.
_orig_newton = authors_quantiles.newton


def _safe_newton(func, x0, fprime=None, *args, **kwargs):
    x0 = np.asarray(x0)
    if x0.size == 0:
        return x0
    return _orig_newton(func, x0, fprime=fprime, *args, **kwargs)


authors_quantiles.newton = _safe_newton

target.statement: Empirical specificity of the proposed full method for IID standard normal errors, mean function μ1, and n=50.
target.dataset: Simulated IID standard normal time series, mean function μ1, n=50, no outliers

tolerance.why: Rule 2: this is an accuracy-like % metric evaluated over 1,000 series × 550 time points (well over 2,000 observations), and the paper prints it as a percentage.

audit_summary: The C1 match target is reproduced by a thin wrapper around the authors' released code: 1000 no-outlier mu1/N(0,1/20) series, n=50, horizon 550, full parallel_test, 5-fold CV bandwidth, PWM GEV threshold at alpha=1%, giving 98.37% per-point specificity versus the paper's 98.3% (0.07 pp). The run is not scaled down: it used all 1000 series and 500 test points per series, with a per-series audit CSV. No paper number is hardcoded; the reference 98.3 is read from the contract only for comparison, and the reported '100.0' occurrences are percentage conversion constants. Documented deviations are minor/paper-underspecified: the authors' repo mu1 variant (A15), PWM/sliding-block GEV choices (A17), and alpha=0.01 per the paper rather than the repo v2's 0.05 (A14); the SciPy empty-start shim is a compatibility fix, not a formula change. Extra claims C2, C4, and C5 match within tolerance, while extra C3 sensitivity is 78.32 versus 80.4 and is explicitly disclosed as not_reproduced; real-data claims C6-C8 were not attempted.

requirement_check.evidence: c1_runner.generate_one_series uses the authors' data_generation.generate_data to build X_i=mu1(i/n)+eps_i; run_one_series_general can add c_i outliers to the test window.
The authors' experiments.parallel_test / jackknife use the one-sided quartic kernel K(x)=15/8(1-x^2)^2 on [-1,0]; each local fit uses only observations up to time i.
The authors' jackknife_estimation implements the Jackknife bias reduction tilde mu=2 hat mu_{h/sqrt2}-hat mu_h.
parallel_test compares |X_i - jackknife estimate| to quantiles.get_quantile at alpha=0.01, implementing rule (5).
The authors' quantiles.get_quantile estimates GEV parameters from the initial n residuals using PWM, which Assumption 6 permits.
Bandwidth and GEV estimation use data[:n_stable]; in contaminated runs, outliers are placed only at indices n_stable..n_total-1, keeping the first n clean.
alpha is passed as a constant 0.01 array for the consecutive tests, matching the Corollary 8(i) constant-level setup.
The authors' jackknife.get_kernel is the one-sided quartic kernel; the wrapper uses it through the authors' code.
bandwidth_cv(data[:n], num_folds=5, min_bw=2, max_bw=20) implements 5-fold CV with MSE loss.
ALPHA=0.01 in c1_runner; metrics config records alpha=0.01.
run_one_series_general draws int(0.05*(11n-n)) outliers in the test window with sign*U(1,2) times the authors' get_minimal_height; used for extra claims C3-C5, not C1.
